correctness.rationale: An invariant simplex gives a simplex of fixed barycenters of its vertex orbits. A nontrivial two-point reflection orbit is an admissible fixed vertex precisely when 2 min(θ,π−θ)<r, hence for r≤π it is either low (θ<r/2) attached to p=0, or high (θ>π−r/2) attached to q=π. Every low–high cross distance is strictly >π−r/2≥r when r≤2π/3, forbidding a connecting simplex. For r>2π/3 up to π, choose θ∈(0,min(r/2,3r/2−π)), then φ∈(π−r/2,r−θ), giving low–high cross-simplex and a p-to-q path; r>π gives a full simplex. Equality is disconnected due to strict < convention. Fixed endpoints of any equivariant path force the path to lie in fixed points, so disconnectivity makes equivariant TC infinite. All cases follow exact inequalities, no numerical extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Colman–Grant give the standard disconnected-fixed-set obstruction to equivariant topological complexity. The September 2026 Daundkar–Sarkar–Singh primary article treats persistent equivariant invariants and (in §3–4) spheres under reflection, but its Proposition 3.9 and 4.3 treat equivariant LS category/TC of persistence intervals for spheres in n≥2 and give no exact fixed-point connectivity classification for the geodesic S1 at strict 2π/3. Complete primary PDF was accessed and its main results checked in this run, eliminating the prior abstract-only access risk. The boundary r=2π/3 is the additional exact claim.
